facts.text: Virtual validation means collecting evidence that a system meets its safety requirements through simulation and laboratory-bench testing instead of, or before, testing the complete real machine.
facts.quote: Virtual validation means collecting evidence that a system meets its safety requirements by testing it in simulation and on laboratory benches instead of, or before, testing the complete real machine.

facts.text: Virtual validation can run very large numbers of situations, repeat them exactly, include dangerous cases that would not be staged with a real worker, and begin long before a prototype exists.
facts.quote: It can run very large numbers of situations, repeat them exactly, include dangerous cases that nobody would stage with a real worker, and start long before the prototype exists.

facts.text: Virtual validation alone cannot prove that a camera will detect a worker through real dust when the dust model and camera model are themselves unproven.
facts.quote: It cannot, by itself, prove that a camera will see a worker through real dust, because the dust model and the camera model are themselves unproven

facts.text: Virtual validation cannot prove that a loaded hauler stops within the predicted distance on wet gravel because the booklet found no validated braking-distance model for heavy machines on loose surfaces.
facts.quote: it cannot prove that a loaded hauler stops in the predicted distance on wet gravel, because no validated braking-distance model for heavy machines on loose surfaces was found

facts.text: The documented validation programs use virtual methods as filters rather than substitutes for physical testing: define the operating domain and scenarios, verify the logic virtually at scale, confirm with fewer physical tests, and release in stages with field monitoring.
facts.quote: use virtual methods as filters, not substitutes: define the operating domain and scenarios first; verify the logic virtually at scale; confirm with a smaller set of physical tests; release in stages with field monitoring

facts.text: Every simulation credibility framework checked by the booklet, spanning aviation, nuclear power and road-vehicle regulation, requires physical anchoring: physical baseline tests validate models, simulation covers the interior of the validated domain, and physical confirmation remains necessary at boundaries and after influential changes.
facts.quote: requires physical anchoring: baseline physical tests validate the model, simulation fills the interior of the validated domain, and physical confirmation stays at the boundaries and after influential changes

facts.text: Regulatory acceptance of virtual validation evidence identified by the booklet is limited to on-road applications.
facts.quote: Acceptance of virtual evidence by regulators is on-road only.

facts.text: Euro NCAP's March 2025 virtual-testing protocol accepts a manufacturer's predictions for a scenario grid if randomly selected grid cells pass physical verification.
facts.quote: Euro NCAP's virtual-testing protocol (March 2025) accepts a manufacturer's predictions for a scenario grid if randomly selected cells pass physical verification.

facts.text: The booklet found no off-road standard or regulator that accepts simulation in place of physical tests for collision avoidance or automatic braking.
facts.quote: No off-road standard or regulator was found that accepts simulation in place of physical tests for collision avoidance or automatic braking

facts.text: Compressing validation from three or four years to under four months is credible only if the virtual pipeline—scenario library, replay adapters, software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test suites, and correlated models—is finished before the prototype arrives, making the four months a confirmation campaign rather than the first iteration of the method.
facts.quote: Compressing validation from three or four years to under four months is credible only if the virtual pipeline (scenario library, replay adapters, software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test suites, correlated models) is finished before the prototype arrives

facts.text: The booklet found no case of an off-road manufacturer validating a new perception-based braking function in under four months.
facts.quote: No case was found of an off-road manufacturer validating a new perception-based braking function in under four months
